name: Belogorka Gorge
near: The village of Belogorka/Konush at the mouth of the gorge (~1.8 km from the catalog's previous point, OSM); the district center is Sokuluk (too.kg: the gorge is “above the village of Sokuluk”). From the waterfall to the last villages it is ~20 km along the valley.
elev: The Belogorka waterfall is at about 2200 m above sea level (open.kg); the drop is about 60 m (too.kg, open.kg, travelbar.kg).
short: Belogorka is a picturesque rocky gorge of the Sokuluk River ~50–80 km west/southwest of Bishkek with the 60 m Belogorka waterfall — one of the highest in northern Kyrgyzstan.
desc: The Belogorka Gorge is a section of the Sokuluk River valley on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too, above the village of Sokuluk. The gorge is notable for its abundance of tall cliffs (a recognizable peak, the “Black Spire”), springs and streams; the slopes have Turkestan birch, hawthorn and wild currant, and there are wild boar, ibex and wolves (open.kg). The main attraction is the Belogorka waterfall, about 60 m high at ~2200 m: the water, as it falls, almost never reaches the ground, turning into a cloud of spray that you can feel from 200 m away (too.kg, open.kg). The origin of the powerful stream is a mystery — there is neither a glacier nor a snowfield above the waterfall. 1.5–2 h of walking higher up is a second waterfall of 7–8 m; experienced hikers go further to the Sokuluk Pass into the West Karakol valley. There is no infrastructure: no signal, no cafes, no accommodation.
guide: Belogorka is the best “one-day” waterfall west of Bishkek: 3 km of an almost flat trail along the river and 60 meters of water breaking into a cloud of spray. Come in May–June, when the waterfall is full — by the end of summer the flow weakens noticeably. Bring a rain jacket: the spray reaches 200 m, and on a sunny day there is a rainbow in it. If you want more, a steep trail for another 2 hours uphill leads to a viewpoint and a small waterfall. There is no signal or shops in the gorge — bring food and water.
see: The Belogorka waterfall (~60 m) and the cloud of spray with a rainbow; the small waterfall of 7–8 m higher up the gorge; the cliffs and the “Black Spire” peak; the Sokuluk River valley, birch groves and meadows; for the experienced — Sokuluk Pass to West Karakol.
skip: You have a low sedan and aren't ready to walk extra kilometers — the road up the gorge is bad. You are going at the end of summer — the waterfall is low on water. You need cafes, a signal and accommodation — the gorge has none of these.
diff: Easy: from the parking area 3 km one way, ~1 h 10 min, ascent ~200–250 m, 2 out of 5 on the hiking.kg scale (the overall trip rating is 4 out of 5 because of the road); the last climb to the waterfall is steeper. The continuation to the viewpoint is a steep trail for another ~2 h (ionlytakepics).
when: May–June — the waterfall is fullest (hiking.kg); in summer you can swim in the river (open.kg). At the end of summer there is little water (ionlytakepics, 2021). In winter the road and trail are not maintained.
hours: A natural area, no time restrictions; the sources do not mention any fee-collection points.
daytime: On a sunny day before lunch a rainbow is visible in the spray; after sunset the waterfall looks like “gray smoke” (open.kg). Leave Bishkek early: the drive takes ~2–2.5 h.
how: From Bishkek west along the Kara-Balta highway to Sokuluk, then turn south along the Sokuluk River (70 km, 2 h 30 min — hiking.kg). The road in the gorge gets worse; sedans are left before the last bridge, and a car with high clearance can drive closer. From the parking area it is 3 km on foot.
needcar: Yes: no public transport runs into the gorge (too.kg). You need a car with high clearance, a taxi or a group tour.
self: Yes, if you have a car with high clearance and an offline map: the trail along the river is clear. Without a car it is easier with a group tour (Travelbar, TUK).
roadtype: Paved road to Sokuluk; up the gorge a dirt road whose quality deteriorates (high clearance needed, too.kg); the last section is a foot trail along the river.
traveltime: Bishkek → parking: 70 km, 2 h 30 min (hiking.kg); travelbar — ~2 h by bus. Parking → waterfall: 3 km, 1 h 10 min (hiking.kg).
stay: There is no accommodation in the gorge (too.kg); there are convenient spots for tents by the waterfall. The nearest hotels are in Sokuluk and Bishkek (specific places not checked).
net: There is no mobile signal in the gorge (too.kg).
entry: An entry fee or eco fee is not mentioned in the sources (too.kg, hiking.kg, travelbar, ionlytakepics); there is no official confirmation that it is free.
transfer: Travelbar.kg group tour — 380 som per person (transport + guide; the date of the listing is not given). Taxi prices Bishkek — Belogorka were not found.
bring: Shoes with a grippy sole, a rain jacket/windbreaker against the spray, a warm layer, water (there are few springs, drinking from the river is not recommended — too.kg), a snack, a first-aid kit, SPF cream (travelbar). For an overnight stay — a tent.
warn: There is no signal — tell acquaintances your route. The rocks at the waterfall are wet and slippery. Wild boar and wolves live in the gorge (open.kg). The road is limited for sedans. Don't drink the river water.
food: There are no cafes or shops in the gorge (too.kg) — the classic format is a picnic by the river (Travelbar and YouTravel tours include a picnic). The nearest cafes are in Sokuluk.
reviews: There is no separate reliable Google Maps listing for the gorge (meta: “ambiguous result”). Tourist reviews (ionlytakepics, otzovik about the “Pigeon Waterfall in Sokuluk”, YouTube): pros — a powerful waterfall, an easy trail, cliffs; cons — a bad road, little water at the end of summer. The hiking.kg rating is 7/10.
p.sum: Belogorka is the highest waterfall in northern Kyrgyzstan (~60 m), ~70–80 km and 2–2.5 h from Bishkek: through Sokuluk and the villages of Belogorka/Konush, then along a worsening dirt road. Sedans are left at the last bridge, and a car with high clearance can drive closer; from the parking spot it is 3 km and ~1 h 10 min along an easy trail by the river. Public transport does not run into the gorge: bus No. 32 only takes you as far as Sokuluk (35 som), so the realistic options are your own car or a taxi with a wait, or a group hike (Travelbar 380 som, TUK, Master Tour). The gorge has no signal, cafe or accommodation — bring water and food, and you can sleep in a tent.
p.apps.0.title: From Bishkek via Sokuluk and Belogorka (the only road route)
p.apps.0.route: Bishkek → Kara-Balta highway → Sokuluk → turn south along the Sokuluk River → Belogorka/Konush village → dirt road up the gorge → last bridge (parking for sedans) → trail to the waterfall
p.apps.0.surface: Paved road to Sokuluk and the villages; up the gorge a stony dirt road, worse toward the end (clearance needed); the last section is a foot trail between a 100+ m cliff and the river
p.apps.0.vehicle: crossover / 4×4; a sedan — up to the last bridge
p.apps.0.season: May to October; May–June the waterfall is fullest; in winter the road is not maintained
p.apps.0.last: Fuel stations, ATMs, shops and cafes — in Sokuluk; no services beyond that. No signal in the gorge
p.apps.0.parking.d: An informal parking spot at the last bridge (sedans); a high-clearance car can go closer to the start of the trail
p.apps.0.parking.price: free (the sources do not mention fees)
p.apps.0.trail.d: End of the road / last bridge: a 3 km trail along the river to the waterfall
p.apps.0.haz: No signal, wet rocks at the waterfall, wild boar and wolves (open.kg). After rain the road turns to mud
p.transport.0.details: 25 buses a day, 10–14 min interval; from there the gorge is another 25–30 km, only by taxi/private driver
p.transport.0.price: 35 som outside the city, 20 som within Bishkek

p.transport.1.details: Agree on a round trip with a 3–4 h wait: there is no signal, so you can't call a car for the way back
p.transport.2.details: Group hike to the waterfall, a bus for up to 36 seats, guide, picnic
p.transport.4.details: Hikes every weekend (Belogorka — regularly), ~2 h of driving

p.iti.0.title: A day from Bishkek
p.iti.0.plan: 7:30 set off → 10:00 parking at the last bridge → 11:15 waterfall, picnic → (optional) 12:00–14:00 upper viewpoint → 15:30 parking → 18:00 Bishkek. With the Sputnik8 tour you can add the Ak-Suu mineral springs
p.iti.1.title: 2 days with a tent
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: arrive after lunch, camp by the waterfall. Day 2: sunrise at the waterfall, climb to the viewpoint, return
p.iti.2.title: What to combine
p.iti.2.plan: The Sokuluk Gorge and the Ak-Suu/Tash-Bulak springs; further west along the highway — Too-Ashuu Pass and Suusamyr (via Kara-Balta, ≈1.5 h from Sokuluk)
p.season: May–June: the waterfall is fullest, the road may be muddy. July–August: warm, swimming is possible, less water. September–October: little water, autumn colors. In winter the road and trail are not maintained
p.budget.economy: ≈400–1000 som: a group hike 380 som (Travelbar) or up to 690–900 som with other operators; your own food
p.budget.comfort: An individual tour €270 per group (Tripster) / £170 per person (Expedia) / $345 per 4×4 car (Sputnik8)
p.permits: No permits or fees needed: the sources do not mention an entry fee or eco fee
p.access: The trail is easy, suitable for families with children (Tripster). Strollers and people with limited mobility — no. Without a car with clearance, a section of the road will have to be walked. Dogs — allowed, but wild boar and wolves live in the gorge
